subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: What lifecycle contract should OpenClaw support for reviewing, editing, forgetting, tombstoning, superseding, and resolving conflicts across memory plugins?
rationale: The code gap is real, but the durable storage model, plugin API boundary, privacy behavior, rollback guarantees, and operator UX are product choices that automation cannot safely pick.

options.title: Define lifecycle contract first
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle schema and plugin API semantics, then split implementation across schema, provenance, write path, and operator surfaces.

options.title: Limit v1 to memory-core
options.body: Implement review/edit/forget/conflict behavior only for the bundled memory-core path and defer external plugin alignment.

options.title: Defer lifecycle MVP
options.body: Keep current search, promotion, and dreaming behavior while tracking concrete stale-memory symptoms separately until lifecycle work is prioritized.

recommendation.title: Define lifecycle contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad design tracker, settle schema and plugin API semantics, then split implementation across schema, provenance, write path, and operator surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory storage and memory SDK provenance work makes this the best available routing candidate for the contract decision.
